idiom_name: Vapor Content/Codable model + ResponseEncodable per media type, Leaf for HTML
implementation_notes: One Content (Codable) struct is the model: Vapor's ContentConfiguration selects the encoder for the request's media type (JSON by default, plus URL-encoded form, multipart, plaintext and HTML entries) and a type conforming to ResponseEncodable can set its own Content-Type, which is how a Leaf-rendered HTML representation joins the JSON and form representations of the same model. Custom representations are added as coders registered on ContentConfiguration or as ResponseEncodable wrappers, replacing the classic view registry with the coder table. The attached-observer form is only needed in a non-server UIKit/SwiftUI app where one model object drives several live views through Observation or Combine.
pitfalls: Codable conformance means every property added to the model changes every serialized representation at once; versioning or hiding fields requires a separate DTO per representation.
A custom ContentEncoder receives the HTTPHeaders inout and must set the Content-Type itself, otherwise clients interpret the body by the wrong media type.
The EventLoopFuture-based and async ResponseEncodable paths coexist: mixing them in one route collection produces 'cannot convert' errors that point at the wrong handler.
